# Acknowledgments

We would like to express our gratitude to the many individuals and organizations that have contributed to the development and success of Rhema.

## Core Team

The Rhema project is maintained by the team at Fugue AI, with contributions from developers, researchers, and community members around the world.

## Contributors

We are grateful to all the contributors who have helped make Rhema what it is today. You can see the full list of contributors in our [GitHub contributors page](https://github.com/fugue-ai/rhema/graphs/contributors).

### Special Thanks

We would like to give special recognition to:

- **Early Adopters**: Those who believed in the project from the beginning and provided valuable feedback
- **Bug Reporters**: Community members who help us identify and fix issues
- **Documentation Contributors**: Those who help make Rhema more accessible through better documentation
- **Code Reviewers**: Contributors who ensure code quality through thorough reviews

## Open Source Dependencies

Rhema is built on the shoulders of many excellent open source projects. We would like to acknowledge the following key dependencies:

### Rust Ecosystem
- **Tokio**: Asynchronous runtime for Rust
- **Serde**: Serialization framework
- **Clap**: Command line argument parsing
- **Tracing**: Application-level tracing
- **Anyhow**: Error handling utilities

### Data Processing
- **Arrow**: Columnar in-memory analytics
- **DataFusion**: SQL query engine
- **Parquet**: Columnar storage format

### Networking & Communication
- **Tonic**: gRPC framework for Rust
- **Prost**: Protocol Buffers implementation
- **Hyper**: HTTP implementation

### Development Tools
- **Cargo**: Rust package manager
- **Clippy**: Rust linter
- **Rustfmt**: Code formatter

## Research & Inspiration

Rhema draws inspiration from various research areas and existing systems:

- **Distributed Systems**: Research on consensus protocols, fault tolerance, and distributed coordination
- **Stream Processing**: Work on real-time data processing and event streaming
- **AI/ML Systems**: Research on intelligent automation and agent-based systems
- **DevOps & CI/CD**: Best practices in continuous integration and deployment

We are grateful for the support from:

- **Rust Community**: The vibrant Rust ecosystem and its helpful community

## How to Contribute

If you would like to be acknowledged in future versions of this file, please consider:

1. **Contributing Code**: Submit pull requests with bug fixes or new features
2. **Reporting Issues**: Help us identify and fix problems
3. **Improving Documentation**: Make Rhema more accessible to others
4. **Spreading the Word**: Share Rhema with your network
5. **Providing Feedback**: Let us know how we can improve

## Recognition Process

Contributors are recognized in several ways:

- **GitHub Contributors**: All code contributors appear in our GitHub contributors graph
- **Release Notes**: Significant contributions are mentioned in release notes
- **Documentation**: Contributors are credited in relevant documentation
- **This File**: Special acknowledgments for exceptional contributions

## Contact

If you believe you should be acknowledged here or if you notice any omissions, please [open an issue](https://github.com/fugue-ai/rhema/issues) or contact us directly.

Thank you to everyone who has contributed to making Rhema a better project!
